purpose: Parts 28 and 29 — measure partner-people evidence and the LinkedIn/public-indexed source family, rather than assuming either.
method: One name-scoped public web search per account combining the company name with partner/channel/alliance role vocabulary. No LinkedIn login, no scraping, no bypassing of access controls — only what a search engine has indexed and returns publicly.
populationChoice: Accounts with an ESTABLISHED partner motion. This is deliberately the MOST FAVOURABLE population: if a company runs a partner programme, a partner person is most likely to exist. A result here is therefore an upper bound on what this method achieves across the corpus, and is reported as such.
priorBelief: An earlier phase measured public person discovery at 2 of 18 and the capability was dropped as non-viable. That measurement is on the frozen list. This test does not tune anything; it measures whether the conclusion holds for the INDEXED-LinkedIn route as opposed to direct access.

finding: Public INDEXED LinkedIn yields named partner people on 7 of 8 accounts, and two or more on 4 of 8. The frozen belief that public person discovery is non-viable was measured at 2/18 — but that measurement is not comparable to this one, because the failure mode there was ACCESS and the route here is a search index that returns LinkedIn profile summaries without ever touching LinkedIn directly. Zero of eight were blocked.
againstInterest: n=8, and the population was chosen to be the most favourable available. This is an upper bound, not a corpus rate.
Four of the eight yield only ONE person, and the mandate's prior rule of thumb was two or more. At the 2+ threshold the rate is 50%, not 87.5%.
One result (Channable) is a snippet describing partnership activity without a stated title — counted as found, which is generous.
One result (DataCore) names a person at a subsidiary brand, which is a brand-resolution risk rather than a clean match.
This measures FINDING a person. It does not measure whether the person is current, still in role, or reachable — none of which was checked.
LinkedIn contributed ZERO unique CRM evidence and ZERO unique partner-programme evidence across the whole project. Its entire measured value is people.
